questions.sec: Adrenal medulla: development, catecholamines and biosynthesis · p852
questions.q: Match adrenal embryology — 1) Adrenal medulla  2) Adrenal cortex … A) Mesoderm (80%)  B) Neuroectoderm (20%)
questions.exp: Medulla (20%) is neuroectodermal; cortex (80%) mesodermal; development completed by the 45th day of IUL. (Book p852)

questions.sec: Adrenal medulla: development, catecholamines and biosynthesis · p852
questions.q: Adrenal development is completed by the ___ day of intra-uterine life.
questions.exp: Development is completed on the 45th day of IUL. (Book p852)

questions.sec: Adrenal medulla: development, catecholamines and biosynthesis · p852
questions.q: By the 80/20 rule, adrenaline (epinephrine) forms what share of medullary catecholamines?
questions.exp: Adrenaline/epinephrine 80% (smaller granules), noradrenaline/norepinephrine 20% (larger dense granules); secretion is pulsatile. (Book p852)

questions.sec: Adrenal medulla: development, catecholamines and biosynthesis · p852
questions.q: Match catecholamine to metabolite — 1) Adrenaline  2) Dopamine  3) Noradrenaline … A) Homovanillic acid (HVA)  B) Normetanephrine  C) Metanephrine and VMA
questions.exp: Adrenaline → metanephrine/VMA; dopamine → HVA; noradrenaline → normetanephrine (metabolites are easier to measure). (Book p852)

questions.sec: Adrenal medulla: development, catecholamines and biosynthesis · p852
questions.q: The rate-limiting step of catecholamine biosynthesis (tyrosine → DOPA) is catalysed by ___.
questions.exp: Tyrosine hydroxylase is the rate-limiting step; the ladder is tyrosine → DOPA → dopamine → NE → epinephrine. (Book p852)

questions.sec: Adrenal medulla: development, catecholamines and biosynthesis · p852
questions.q: The enzyme converting norepinephrine to epinephrine is:
questions.exp: PNMT (phenylethanolamine N-methyltransferase) converts NE to epinephrine. (Book p852)

questions.sec: Adrenal medulla: development, catecholamines and biosynthesis · p852
questions.q: ‘PNMT is present only in the adrenal gland, so extra-adrenal pheochromocytomas produce only norepinephrine.’
opts: False — extra-adrenal tumours make only epinephrine
questions.exp: PNMT is adrenal-only; extra-adrenal pheochromocytoma lacks it and produces only NE. (Book p852)

questions.sec: Adrenal medulla: development, catecholamines and biosynthesis · p852
questions.q: The metabolic relation between cortex and medulla is:
questions.exp: Cortisol from the cortex stimulates medullary PNMT. (Book p852)

questions.sec: Adrenomedullin, pheochromocytoma definition and the types tree · p853
questions.q: Adrenomedullin is produced from the:
questions.exp: Adrenomedullin is produced from endothelium; it causes vasodilation and inhibits endothelial cell apoptosis (prevents septic shock). (Book p853)

questions.sec: Adrenomedullin, pheochromocytoma definition and the types tree · p853
questions.q: The other granule contents of the medulla listed are:
questions.exp: Other contents of granules: opioids and chromogranin A. (Book p853)

questions.sec: Adrenomedullin, pheochromocytoma definition and the types tree · p853
questions.q: Pheochromocytoma typically presents in which decades, with what sex ratio?
questions.exp: Age 4th to 5th decade; male:female 1:1. (Book p853)

questions.sec: Adrenomedullin, pheochromocytoma definition and the types tree · p853
questions.q: Pheochromocytoma is defined as a neural-crest cell tumour producing:
questions.exp: Definition: neural crest cell tumour producing catecholamines (pulsatile) and catecholamine metabolites. (Book p853)

questions.sec: Adrenomedullin, pheochromocytoma definition and the types tree · p853
questions.q: By origin, adrenal pheochromocytoma and extra-adrenal paraganglioma split as:
questions.exp: Adrenal 75%; extra-adrenal pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma 25% with high malignant potential. (Book p853)

questions.sec: Adrenomedullin, pheochromocytoma definition and the types tree · p853
questions.q: The m/c site of sympathetic-ganglia paraganglioma (20%) is the:
questions.exp: Sympathetic ganglia (20%): m/c site organ of Zuckerkandl. (Book p853)

questions.sec: Adrenomedullin, pheochromocytoma definition and the types tree · p853
questions.q: Parasympathetic paragangliomas (5%) are typically non-functional; their m/c site is:
questions.exp: Parasympathetic ganglia (5%): non-functional; m/c site carotid body > jugular bulb. (Book p853)

questions.sec: Adrenomedullin, pheochromocytoma definition and the types tree · p853
questions.q: ‘Page 852 says extra-adrenal tumours secrete only NE (no PNMT), yet the p853 types tree prints ‘produce only NA’ under the adrenal branch and ‘adrenaline > NA’ under extra-adrenal — the PNMT mechanism (p852) is the one to apply in answers.’
opts: False — p852 says adrenal lacks PNMT
True — the tree print conflicts with the PNMT mechanism
questions.exp: The book's own p852 mechanism (PNMT adrenal-only, extra-adrenal = NE only) conflicts with the printed p853 tree labels; learn the mechanism. (Book p853)

questions.sec: Adrenomedullin, pheochromocytoma definition and the types tree · p853
questions.q: The CURRENT statistics that replaced the obsolete ‘rule of 10’ are:
questions.exp: Obsolete rule of 10 = 10% each; current: bilateral 40%, extra-adrenal 25%, familial 40%, malignant 50%. (Book p853)

questions.sec: Adrenomedullin, pheochromocytoma definition and the types tree · p853
questions.q: Familial pheochromocytoma (40% currently) is associated with, and the STRONGEST association is:
questions.exp: Familial cases occur in young patients; associated with MEN (strongest association), VHL (von Hippel-Lindau), NF-1 (neurofibromatosis). (Book p853)

questions.sec: Adrenomedullin, pheochromocytoma definition and the types tree · p853
questions.q: Familial pheochromocytomas are usually bilateral EXCEPT when associated with:
questions.exp: Usually B/L except NF-1 associated (U/L). (Book p853)

questions.sec: Adrenomedullin, pheochromocytoma definition and the types tree · p853
questions.q: The surest sign of malignant pheochromocytoma and the mutation raising metastatic potential are:
questions.exp: Surest sign = metastasis; SDH-B ↑ metastatic potential. (Book p853)

questions.sec: Pheochromocytoma pathophysiology and clinical features · p854
questions.q: Sustained sympathetic activity in pheochromocytoma leads to:
opts: ↑ intravascular volume, DM and weight loss
questions.exp: Leads to ↑ intravascular volume (with ↓GFR → hypercalcaemia → acute abdominal pain, and postural hypotension), DM and weight loss. (Book p854)

questions.sec: Pheochromocytoma pathophysiology and clinical features · p854
questions.q: Pheochromocytoma causes 2° paraneoplastic polycythaemia by producing:
questions.exp: Pheochromocytoma produces erythropoietin (EPO) → 2° paraneoplastic polycythemia. (Book p854)

questions.sec: Pheochromocytoma pathophysiology and clinical features · p854
questions.q: The m/c symptom of the classic triad — episodic headache — occurs in:
questions.exp: Triad: episodic headache (95%, m/c symptom), palpitation/tachycardia, profuse sweating. (Book p854)

questions.sec: Pheochromocytoma pathophysiology and clinical features · p854
questions.q: The other two corners of the symptom triad are:
questions.exp: Palpitation/tachycardia and profuse sweating complete the triad. (Book p854)

questions.sec: Pheochromocytoma pathophysiology and clinical features · p854
questions.q: Pallor during spells in pheochromocytoma should raise suspicion of:
questions.exp: Pallor: suspect malignancy. Other features: abdominal pain, palpitation (sinus tachy), perspiration, panic attack (75%), postural hypotension, weight loss, hyperadrenergic spells. (Book p854)

questions.sec: Pheochromocytoma pathophysiology and clinical features · p854
questions.q: The m/c SIGN — episodic hypertension — is seen in:
questions.exp: Episodic hypertension (75–85%) is the m/c sign; sustained only in 20%, giving resistant young hypertension. (Book p854)

questions.sec: Pheochromocytoma pathophysiology and clinical features · p854
questions.q: Sustained hypertension occurs in only:
questions.exp: Sustained only in 20% — resistant young hypertension. (Book p854)

questions.sec: Pheochromocytoma pathophysiology and clinical features · p854
questions.q: Normal BP between spells is found in:
questions.exp: Normal BP in 15%. (Book p854)

questions.sec: Pheochromocytoma pathophysiology and clinical features · p854
questions.q: Match postural hypotension criteria (any one) — 1) Heart rate  2) Systolic BP  3) Diastolic BP … A) ↓ >20 mmHg  B) ↑ >30/min  C) ↓ >10 mmHg
questions.exp: Supine then standing (2–5 min): ↑HR >30/min, ↓systolic >20 mmHg or ↓diastolic >10 mmHg = postural hypotension (75%). (Book p854)

questions.sec: Incidentaloma, cardiac effects and first investigations · p855
questions.q: Among benign adrenal incidentalomas, the functional tumour order is:
questions.exp: Benign (m/c) incidentalomas are endocrine-inactive or functional; functional: cortisol-producing > pheochromocytoma. (Book p855)

questions.sec: Incidentaloma, cardiac effects and first investigations · p855
questions.q: The alarm signs in a NON-functioning adrenal tumour prompting adrenalectomy (any one) are:
opts: Size >4 cm, CT density >20 HU, CT contrast washout <40%
questions.exp: Alarm signs: size >4 cm; CT density >20 HU; CT contrast washout <40% — any 1 (+) → adrenalectomy. (Book p855)

questions.sec: Incidentaloma, cardiac effects and first investigations · p855
questions.q: Catecholamine excess affects the heart by raising:
opts: Rate, excitability, O2 consumption and force
questions.exp: Heart: ↑ rate, ↑ excitability, ↑ O2 consumption, ↑ force. (Book p855)

questions.sec: Incidentaloma, cardiac effects and first investigations · p855
questions.q: Pheochromocytoma is a named cause of which cardiomyopathy (the other being sarcoidosis)?
questions.exp: Cause for dilated cardiomyopathy (other cause: sarcoidosis). (Book p855)

questions.sec: Incidentaloma, cardiac effects and first investigations · p855
questions.q: Which is NOT in the book's hypercalcaemia-associated disease list?
questions.exp: Listed: Addison's disease, pheochromocytoma, thyrotoxicosis, acromegaly — not Cushing's. (Book p855)

questions.sec: Incidentaloma, cardiac effects and first investigations · p855
questions.q: ‘The m/c cause of panic attack is NOT pheochromocytoma.’
questions.exp: Note: m/c cause of panic attack is not pheochromocytoma (though panic attack occurs in 75% of pheo patients). (Book p855)

questions.sec: Incidentaloma, cardiac effects and first investigations · p855
questions.q: The histopathology pattern of pheochromocytoma is the ___.
questions.exp: Histopathology: Zellballen pattern. (Book p855)

questions.sec: Incidentaloma, cardiac effects and first investigations · p855
questions.q: The immunohistochemical markers listed are:
questions.exp: Markers: chromogranin, synaptophysin, S100. (Book p855)

questions.sec: Incidentaloma, cardiac effects and first investigations · p855
questions.q: Before biochemical testing, which drugs must be stopped because they interfere?
questions.exp: Stop tricyclic antidepressants, L-Dopa and NSAIDs before testing (they interfere with the test). (Book p855)

questions.sec: Biochemical screening, imaging and surgical TOC · p856
questions.q: The SCREENING test for pheochromocytoma (98% sensitivity and specificity) is:
questions.exp: 24 hr fractionated metanephrine/NM is the screening test with 98% sensitivity and 98% specificity. (Book p856)

questions.sec: Biochemical screening, imaging and surgical TOC · p856
questions.q: Plasma fractionated metanephrine/NM has what sensitivity (no false negatives)?
questions.exp: Plasma fractionated metanephrine/NM: 100% sensitivity; done along with 24 hr urine if very strong family history. (Book p856)

questions.sec: Biochemical screening, imaging and surgical TOC · p856
questions.q: The IOC for adrenal pheochromocytoma on imaging is:
questions.exp: MRI abdomen is IOC, showing T2 hyperintensities with hemorrhagic/cystic changes. (Book p856)

questions.sec: Biochemical screening, imaging and surgical TOC · p856
questions.q: Which two imaging modalities are now obsolete?
questions.exp: MIBG and FDG-PET are obsolete now. (Book p856)

questions.sec: Biochemical screening, imaging and surgical TOC · p856
questions.q: Gallium DOTATATE PET scan is the IOC when:
opts: MRI is negative but biochemical tests are positive (paraganglioma)
questions.exp: Ga-DOTATATE PET is IOC if MRI negative but biochemically positive (paraganglioma). (Book p856)

questions.sec: Biochemical screening, imaging and surgical TOC · p856
questions.q: The DOTATATE principle is: DOTA–octreotate binds to:
opts: Somatostatin receptor type 2 (SSTR2) on the tumour surface
questions.exp: DOTA → octreotate binds somatostatin receptor type 2 on the tumour surface. (Book p856)

questions.sec: Biochemical screening, imaging and surgical TOC · p856
questions.q: The treatment of choice for pheochromocytoma is:
questions.exp: Laparoscopic retroperitoneal adrenalectomy is TOC. (Book p856)

questions.sec: Biochemical screening, imaging and surgical TOC · p856
questions.q: Pre-surgical preparation begins how many days before surgery (admit + liberal fluids)?
questions.exp: 10 days before surgery: admit patient and give liberal fluid intake (then BP control). (Book p856)

questions.sec: Pre-operative blockade and intraoperative crisis · p857
questions.q: The DOC α-blocker for pre-operative BP control is:
questions.exp: Phenoxybenzamine (10 mg OD step-up to 10 mg TDS): non-selective, irreversible, long-lasting, non-competitive inhibitor. (Book p857)

questions.sec: Pre-operative blockade and intraoperative crisis · p857
questions.q: Phenoxybenzamine is best described as a:
questions.exp: It is non-selective, irreversible, long-lasting and non-competitive. (Book p857)

questions.sec: Pre-operative blockade and intraoperative crisis · p857
questions.q: Other α-blockers used, and the step-up dose for prazosin, are:
opts: Prazosin (2.5 mg OD → 5 mg BD) and terazosin
questions.exp: Others: prazosin (2.5 mg OD → 5 mg BD), terazosin. (Book p857)

questions.sec: Pre-operative blockade and intraoperative crisis · p857
questions.q: If adequate BP control is not achieved, the added drug class is:
questions.exp: Ca channel blockers amlodipine/nicardipine if adequate BP control not achieved; metyrosine rarely used. (Book p857)

questions.sec: Pre-operative blockade and intraoperative crisis · p857
questions.q: HR control with β-blockers is added how many days before surgery (atenolol 12.5 mg BD → 25 mg BD)?
questions.exp: 3 days before surgery: β-blockers (atenolol 12.5 mg BD → 25 mg BD) — always after α-blockade. (Book p857)

questions.sec: Pre-operative blockade and intraoperative crisis · p857
questions.q: The intraoperative hypertensive crisis is managed with:
questions.exp: Intraoperative hypertensive crisis: sodium nitroprusside/nicardipine. (Book p857)

questions.sec: Pre-operative blockade and intraoperative crisis · p857
questions.q: Which drug is NOT part of the pre-operative preparation list?
questions.exp: Metyrosine is rarely used, not first-line; phenoxybenzamine DOC, prazosin/terazosin others, atenolol for HR. (Book p857)

units.title: Medullary development, catecholamines and the PNMT rule
units.guide: Medulla = neuroectoderm (20%), cortex = mesoderm (80%); complete by day 45 IUL. Catecholamines pulsatile, 80/20 adrenaline/NA; smaller granules adrenaline, larger dense NA. Metabolites (easier to measure): metanephrine/VMA, HVA, normetanephrine. Synthesis: tyrosine →(tyrosine hydroxylase, rate-limiting) DOPA → dopamine → NE →(PNMT) epinephrine. PNMT adrenal-only → extra-adrenal pheo makes only NE; cortisol stimulates PNMT.

units.title: Adrenomedullin and the pheochromocytoma types tree
units.guide: Adrenomedullin (endothelium): vasodilation, inhibits endothelial apoptosis (prevents septic shock); granules also contain opioids, chromogranin A. Pheo: 4th–5th decade, M=F; neural-crest tumour making catecholamines + metabolites. Adrenal 75% vs extra-adrenal paraganglioma 25% (high malignant potential; sympathetic 20% organ of Zuckerkandl; parasympathetic 5% non-functional carotid body > jugular bulb). Rule of 10 obsolete; current bilateral 40/extra-adrenal 25/familial 40/malignant 50. Familial: MEN strongest, VHL, NF-1; B/L except NF-1. Malignancy: metastasis surest; SDH-B ↑ metastatic potential. Book conflict: p853 tree labels vs p852 PNMT mechanism.

units.title: Pathophysiology, the triad and BP patterns
units.guide: Sustained sympathetic activity → ↑ intravascular volume (↓GFR → hypercalcaemia → acute abdominal pain; postural hypotension), DM, weight loss; EPO → 2° paraneoplastic polycythaemia. Triad: episodic headache 95% (m/c symptom), palpitation/tachycardia, profuse sweating. Others: abdominal pain, perspiration, panic attack 75%, pallor (suspect malignancy), weight loss, hyperadrenergic spells. Signs: episodic HTN 75–85% (m/c sign; sustained only 20% = resistant young HTN), normal BP 15%, postural hypotension 75% (↑HR >30/min, ↓SBP >20, ↓DBP >10).

units.title: Incidentaloma alarms, cardiac effects, histology and pre-test drugs
units.guide: Benign m/c; functional cortisol-producing > pheo. Non-functioning alarms (any 1 → adrenalectomy): >4 cm, CT >20 HU, washout <40%. Heart ↑ rate/excitability/O2/force; dilated cardiomyopathy (other: sarcoidosis). Hypercalcaemia associates: Addison's, pheo, thyrotoxicosis, acromegaly. m/c cause of panic attack is NOT pheo. Zellballen pattern; markers chromogranin, synaptophysin, S100. Stop TCAs, L-Dopa, NSAIDs before testing.

units.title: Screening, imaging and pre-operative preparation
units.guide: Screening: 24 hr fractionated metanephrine/NM (98%/98%); plasma 100% sensitivity (with urine if strong family history). MRI abdomen IOC (T2 hyperintense, hemorrhagic/cystic); MIBG/FDG-PET obsolete; Ga-DOTATATE PET IOC if MRI −ve but biochemically +ve (SSTR2 binding). TOC laparoscopic retroperitoneal adrenalectomy. 10 days before: admit + liberal fluids + α-blockade (phenoxybenzamine DOC, non-selective irreversible non-competitive; prazosin/terazosin; CCB if needed; metyrosine rarely); 3 days before: β-blocker atenolol; intraop crisis: sodium nitroprusside/nicardipine.
